events.text: The first lesson does not go well. {npc} has watched you train for years and has opinions about all of it. By the second hour you are arguing about how to stand, and by the third you are both laughing too hard to stand at all.

mem.note: started again with me, properly

effects.log: You start again. {npc} holds the stance until {his} legs shake and does not complain once. You are prouder than you say.

choices.text: Let {him} show you how {he} would do it

mem.note: let me teach them something back

effects.log: {npc} shows you. It is wrong, and it is also interesting. You steal one small thing from it for yourself.

choices.text: Call it a night and cook together

mem.note: cooked with me after the first lesson

effects.log: The lesson ends early. The rice burns. It is one of the better evenings of the year.

events.text: {npc} asks for the lesson, not you. "I am tired of watching from the door," {he} says. "If something comes for this house, I want to be standing in front of it too."

mem.note: taught me to breathe before anything else

effects.log: You sit back to back in the courtyard and breathe until the stars come out. It is slower than {npc} wanted, and it is right.

mem.note: taught me to fall a hundred times

effects.log: You teach {npc} to fall, roll and stand, a hundred times. {He} is bruised and furious and better.

choices.text: Tell {him} the truth about what comes for houses like this

mem.note: told me the truth about our enemies

effects.log: You tell {npc} what you have seen. {He} listens to all of it, then picks up the staff again.

events.text: {npc} comes to the yard at dawn, as {he} has since {he} was small. Today you do not correct {his} stance. You hand {him} your own practice sword instead, and wait to see what {he} does with it.

choices.text: Teach the forms you never showed anyone

mem.note: showed me the forms they kept for themselves

effects.log: You show {npc} the forms you kept for yourself. {He} does not ask why now. {He} just learns them.

choices.text: Spar at full speed for the first time

mem.note: sparred with me for real at last

effects.log: You do not hold back, quite. {npc} lasts longer than you expected, and grins through a split lip.

choices.text: Talk about why you fight at all

mem.note: told me why they fight

effects.log: The lesson becomes a long talk under the eaves. {npc} remembers every word of it for years.

events.text: A grown child does not take a lesson the way a small one does. {npc} questions every correction, tries it {his} own way, fails, and then does it yours. It is like teaching yourself, years ago.

mem.note: let me find my own mistake

effects.log: You say nothing. On the fourth try {npc} finds it, and looks up at you, and you nod.

choices.text: Correct {him} at once, as you would a disciple

mem.note: corrected me like a disciple

effects.log: {npc} bristles, then does it right. Later {he} thanks you, a little stiffly.

choices.text: Tell {him} you made the same mistake for ten years

mem.note: admitted making the same mistake

effects.log: {npc} laughs out loud. The lesson goes better after that.

events.text: You lay the scroll on the stone bench, though neither of you needs it. The technique is in your hands, and now it is going into {npc}'s. {He} asks if there is a rule about who it may be taught to.

choices.text: "Only to someone you would die for"

mem.note: told me who an art is for

effects.log: {npc} is quiet for a long while. Then {he} rolls the scroll up and gives it back to you.

mem.note: gave me no rule but deserving

effects.log: {npc} nods. Years later you hear of a stranger {he} saved, and the form {he} used.

choices.text: "Never to an enemy of this house"

mem.note: made me swear it to the house

effects.log: {npc} swears it on the spot, with more ceremony than you meant. You let {him}.

events.text: {npc} learns the technique faster than any disciple you have seen, and you understand why: {he} has watched you use it for years, in the yard, in the dark, once on the road with blood on your sleeve.

choices.text: Tell {him} the story of the road

mem.note: told me the story behind the technique

effects.log: You tell {npc} the whole story. {He} practises the form differently after that, harder.

mem.note: gave me their old training sword

effects.log: {npc} keeps the old sword on the wall and uses it every morning.

choices.text: Spar with it until {he} can turn it on you

mem.note: sparred until I could turn it on them

effects.log: By the end of the season {npc} turns the technique on you, once. You are delighted.

events.text: Whatever your own teachers gave you, or kept from you, does not matter now. {npc} kneels in the yard, and you pass on the technique the way it should be passed: slowly, form by form, with nobody watching.

choices.text: Make {him} copy the forms by hand as well

mem.note: made me copy every form by hand

effects.log: {npc} copies the forms by brush for a month. The copy is better than your own.

choices.text: Tell {him} it is {his} now, to change

mem.note: let me change the technique

effects.log: {npc} changes one form within a year. It is better. You tell nobody that you think so.

choices.text: Teach the counter to it too

mem.note: taught me how it is beaten

effects.log: You teach {npc} how the technique is beaten as well. {He} understands that this is the real gift.

events.text: {npc} asks to learn the technique you used the year the house was threatened. You had not thought {he} remembered. {He} remembers every movement of it.

mem.note: taught me the technique that saved the house

effects.log: You teach {npc} all of it, including the part you have never used since.

mem.note: taught me slowly, to make it hold

effects.log: You teach {npc} one form a month. {He} is impatient, and it holds better for it.

mem.note: asked why I wanted it, and listened

effects.log: "So you do not have to use it again," {npc} says. You have to go and stand in the garden for a while.

events.text: The house shakes before dawn. When you reach the courtyard, {npc} is sitting in the middle of it, surrounded by cracked tiles, at {npc_realm}: a realm above your own. {He} looks up at you, half afraid of what you will say.

mem.note: bowed to me when I passed them

effects.log: You bow, properly, as to a senior. {npc} bursts into tears and then laughs at {him}self for it.

mem.note: asked me to teach them, after

effects.log: {npc} stares, then grins. That evening the lessons in the courtyard go the other way for the first time.

choices.text: Say nothing, and sweep the tiles

mem.note: swept up the tiles with me

effects.log: You sweep the tiles together in silence. It says more than a speech.

events.text: The news reaches you before {npc} does: {npc_realm}, a realm above yours. When {he} comes home {he} stands in the doorway and does not quite know where to put {his} hands.

choices.text: Throw a feast, the whole house

mem.note: threw a feast when I passed them

effects.log: The house feasts. You give the first toast and keep it short, because your voice will not hold.

mem.note: asked me how it felt

effects.log: {npc} tries to tell you. You listen until the lamp burns out, and learn something about your own gate.

mem.note: said they always knew

effects.log: {npc} does not believe you, then does. It is the best thing you say all year.

events.text: {npc}, whom you taught to hold a sword, stands at {npc_realm} now, higher than you. The whole street knows it. Someone at the market asks if it is strange. You think about it.

mem.note: said I was the point of teaching

effects.log: You say it at the market and mean it. The story goes round the town by evening.

mem.note: trained beside me that night

effects.log: You train until the moon goes down. {npc} finds you there and trains beside you without a word.

mem.note: told me the truth, that it stung

effects.log: You admit it to {npc}. {He} laughs, and admits {he} was afraid you would be angry.

events.text: The witnesses have gone. {npc} stands at the gate with one bundle, the way {he} came. The servants pretend to be busy. Neither of you has said the last thing yet.

mem.note: gave me half the silver at the gate

effects.log: You press a heavy purse into {his} hands. {npc} takes it without thanks, which is fair.

mem.note: said sorry at the gate

effects.log: {npc} looks at you for a long moment. "I know," {he} says, and goes.

mem.note: let me go without a word

effects.log: The gate closes. The house is very quiet for a long time.

events.text: {npc} does not cry. {He} folds {his} robes, one by one, and takes down the painting {he} brought on the wedding day. "Keep the rest," {he} says. "I do not want anything from this house."

choices.text: Ask {him} to leave the painting on the wall

mem.note: asked me to leave my painting on the wall

effects.log: {npc} hesitates, then hangs it back on the wall. "For the house," {he} says. "Not for you."

choices.text: Send a servant with {him} for the road

mem.note: sent someone to see me home

effects.log: You send your best servant to see {npc} safely home. {He} does not refuse.

mem.note: threw my faults at me at the gate

effects.log: {npc} goes white, then red, and leaves the painting where it falls.

events.text: The street knows within the hour. By evening there are three versions of why, all wrong. {npc} has gone to an inn across the river and sent back a single line: "Tell the children it was not them."

mem.note: told the children it was not them

effects.log: You gather the children and tell them. The smallest one asks if {npc} still loves them. You say yes.

choices.text: Go to the inn and talk once more

mem.note: came to the inn to talk once more

effects.log: You talk until the inn closes. Nothing is mended, but something is less broken.

mem.note: burned my letter to the children

effects.log: The letter burns. The children are not told anything, and they notice.

events.text: A year on, {npc} finds you alone on the veranda. "Why did you send my other parent away?" {he} asks. {He} has clearly practised the question for a long time.

mem.note: told me the truth about the divorce

effects.log: You tell {npc} the truth, as gently as it goes. {He} does not forgive it tonight, but {he} understands it.

mem.note: said it was their fault

effects.log: {npc} nods slowly. "I thought so," {he} says, and sits closer anyway.

choices.text: Say {he} will understand when {he} is older

mem.note: would not tell me why

effects.log: {npc} goes back inside. {He} does not ask you anything again for a long time.

events.text: {npc} has started visiting {his} other parent across the river, every month, and coming home quiet. Tonight {he} asks if {he} has to choose between you.

mem.note: said I would never have to choose

effects.log: {npc} lets out a breath {he} has been holding for a year. The next visit {he} comes home humming.

choices.text: Go with {him} on the next visit

mem.note: came with me across the river

effects.log: The three of you drink tea in a cramped room across the river. It is awkward and it is good.

mem.note: made me stop visiting

effects.log: {npc} stops going. {He} also stops talking to you at supper.

events.text: Years after the gate closed, you meet {npc} on a bridge in the next town. {He} is greyer, or you are, and for a moment neither of you can think of a single thing to say.

choices.text: Ask how {he} has been, and mean it

mem.note: asked after me on the bridge, and meant it

effects.log: You talk on the bridge until the lanterns are lit. It is not love again. It is something kinder than nothing.

mem.note: bowed to me on the bridge

effects.log: {npc} bows back. That is all, and it is enough.

choices.text: Say what you never said at the gate

mem.note: said at last what they never said

effects.log: You say it. {npc} listens to the end, then says {his} own piece. You both walk home lighter.

events.text: {npc} sends word: {he} is ill, or says {he} is, and would like to see you once. The messenger waits at the door for your answer.

mem.note: came at once when I sent word

effects.log: {npc} is not as ill as {he} said. {He} wanted to see if you would come. You did.

mem.note: sent medicine and a letter

effects.log: You send the best medicine in the market and a careful letter. The reply is short and warm.

mem.note: sent nothing when I was ill

effects.log: The messenger goes away. You think about it more than you expected, for a long time.

events.text: At a wedding in the town you find yourself seated across from {npc}, by someone with a sense of humour. The whole table is watching to see who speaks first.

mem.note: raised a cup to me at the wedding

effects.log: {npc} raises {his} cup back. The table relaxes. Somebody starts a song.

choices.text: Tell the story of your own wedding

mem.note: told the story of our wedding, kindly

effects.log: You tell it, and {npc} corrects the details, and the table cries with laughter.

mem.note: changed seats rather than speak

effects.log: You change seats. {npc} watches you go and says something to the table that makes them laugh.

events.text: The teahouses have a new story, and it is about you and {npc}. A master and a student. By the time it reaches the next province it is a ballad, and not a kind one.

choices.text: Walk through the market with {him}, openly

mem.note: walked through the market with me, openly

effects.log: You walk the length of the market side by side. The whispering does not stop, but it starts to sound different.

choices.text: Go before the elders and answer for it

mem.note: answered for us before the elders

effects.log: You stand before the elders and answer every question. They do not approve. They do not forbid it either.

choices.text: Wait for the talk to die

mem.note: kept us hidden while the talk ran

effects.log: You keep to the house and wait. {npc} waits beside you, and wonders if you are ashamed.

events.text: An old friend from your young days comes to the house, sits down without being asked, and says what everyone is saying: "{npc} was your student. People will say you raised {him} for this."

mem.note: called the gossips fools

effects.log: Your friend shrugs, drinks your tea, and goes away to tell everyone you said it.

mem.note: let me answer for myself

effects.log: {npc} answers, calmly and at length. Your friend leaves impressed, and a little ashamed.

mem.note: admitted the talk worried them

effects.log: You admit it. {npc} hears it through the screen and is quiet with you for days.

events.text: The young people at the practice yard will not meet your eye. One of them finally asks, in front of everyone, whether a student who trains hard enough gets the same reward.

mem.note: answered the yard honestly about us

effects.log: You answer it honestly. The yard is silent, and then, oddly, practice goes on.

choices.text: Send the asker to sweep the steps

mem.note: silenced the yard about us

effects.log: The asker sweeps the steps for a month. Nobody asks again. Nobody forgets either.

choices.text: Ask {npc} to train in the yard as before

mem.note: asked me to train in the yard as before

effects.log: {npc} trains in the yard the next day, and the next. Slowly it stops being strange.

events.text: {npc} says no, and then says nothing else. For a week {he} trains at the far end of the yard. Then {he} comes to your door with tea, as {he} always did, and waits to see if you will take it.

choices.text: Take the tea, and say nothing of it ever again

mem.note: never spoke of it again

effects.log: You take the tea. Neither of you mentions it again, and in a year it is almost as if it never happened.

mem.note: apologised properly

effects.log: You apologise. {npc} bows, accepts it, and goes back to being your student, carefully.

mem.note: closed the door on me

effects.log: You close the door. {npc} stands outside a long time, then goes. The tea goes cold on the step.

events.text: The hall has heard, of course. {npc} is the one they whisper about, not you, and it is not fair. {He} has stopped coming to the evening meal.

choices.text: Tell the hall it was your doing, and only yours

mem.note: took the blame before the hall

effects.log: You say it to the whole hall. The whispering turns on you instead, which is right.

mem.note: brought me a meal when I hid

effects.log: You leave a bowl outside {npc}'s door. The next night {he} comes to the hall again.

mem.note: let the hall whisper about me

effects.log: The whispering runs its course. {npc} never quite looks at you the same way again.
